articles.title: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
articles.snippet: A mystery-shopping experiment found that exchange fees, foreign exchange spreads and banking rails mean stablecoin remittances are often no cheaper than traditional transfer means.

articles.title: Tether posts $1.5 billion operating profit in Q2 as reserve buffer falls by half
articles.snippet: The world’s largest stablecoin issuer added 14 metric tons of gold and about 1,800 bitcoin to its reserves during the second quarter.

articles.title: Bank of Italy finds no consistent cost advantage for stablecoin remittances
articles.snippet: Researchers found that fiat conversion costs and payment infrastructure, rather than blockchain fees, accounted for most of the differences in stablecoin remittance costs and settlement times.

articles.title: Tether earns $1.5B in Q2 as US Treasury holdings fuel profits
articles.snippet: Tether’s reserve surplus grew to $4.11 billion in the second quarter as USDT supply rose despite a weaker stablecoin market and continued pressure across the crypto sector.

articles.title: Tether Reports $1.5B Q2 Profit as USDT Supply Grows, Gold Holdings Rise
articles.snippet: The latest attestation offers a snapshot of the assets backing the world's largest stablecoin, including U.S. Treasuries, repo agreements, and more than 146 metric tons of gold.
